headline: Biman signs deal to buy 11 more Boeing aircraft to expand fleet
summary: The national carrier has ordered five 787-10 Dreamliners and six 737-8 jets to strengthen international connectivity.
details: Biman Bangladesh Airlines has signed a supplemental agreement with Boeing to purchase 11 new aircraft, including five 787-10 Dreamliners and six 737-8 jets.
This order follows a previous purchase of 14 aircraft earlier this year, as part of a broader plan to renew the national carrier's fleet and expand its network.
Biman Chairman Rumee A Hossain stated that the agreement is a key step in responding to specific fleet requirements and improving connectivity for passengers, expatriates, and tourists.
Boeing Senior VP Brad McMullen noted that the additional aircraft will provide the efficiency and reliability needed to support Bangladesh's growing role in global aviation.
The signing ceremony took place on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, attended by high-level officials from both Bangladesh and the United States.
Biman currently operates a mix of 787, 777, and 737 Next-Generation aircraft to connect Bangladesh with hubs in Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

headline: UNGA81: PM calls for urgent global action on climate crisis
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman urges the international community to meet the 1.5-degree Celsius target and ensure predictable climate finance for vulnerable nations.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman called for five urgent global actions to tackle climate change during a high-level meeting at the UN Headquarters in New York on Wednesday.
The Prime Minister urged the international community to achieve the 1.5-degree Celsius global warming limit through emission cuts, as set out in the Paris Agreement.
He called for predictable and accessible finance for adaptation in climate-vulnerable countries and greater access to climate-smart technologies for a just transition.
Tarique Rahman also stressed the need to expand renewable energy through technology transfer and the full implementation of the Loss and Damage Fund.
Highlighting Bangladesh's vulnerability, he stated that the country contributes less than 0.5 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions but faces severe risks.
He warned that Bangladesh could lose 12 to 18 percent of its coastal areas to sea-level rise by the end of the century, affecting tens of millions of people.
The Prime Minister noted that climate change has already caused loss and damage equivalent to 1% of the country's GDP and put food security at serious risk.
Bangladesh has allocated nearly $3.19 billion in its budget for climate adaptation, including plans to plant 250 million trees and dig 20,000 km of rivers and canals.
The government aims to generate 20 percent of its electricity demand from renewable sources by 2030 and is promoting green industries and a national carbon market.
caption:
Bangladesh contributes less than 0.5% of global emissions, yet faces losing up to 18% of its coast. PM Tarique Rahman demands urgent global action.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman called for five urgent global actions to tackle climate change during a high-level meeting at the UN Headquarters in New York on Wednesday.

The Prime Minister urged the international community to achieve the 1.5-degree Celsius global warming limit through emission cuts, as set out in the Paris Agreement.

He called for predictable and accessible finance for adaptation in climate-vulnerable countries and greater access to climate-smart technologies for a just transition.

Tarique Rahman also stressed the need to expand renewable energy through technology transfer and the full implementation of the Loss and Damage Fund.

Highlighting Bangladesh's vulnerability, he stated that the country contributes less than 0.5 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions but faces severe risks.

He warned that Bangladesh could lose 12 to 18 percent of its coastal areas to sea-level rise by the end of the century, affecting tens of millions of people.

The Prime Minister noted that climate change has already caused loss and damage equivalent to 1% of the country's GDP and put food security at serious risk.

Bangladesh has allocated nearly $3.19 billion in its budget for climate adaptation, including plans to plant 250 million trees and dig 20,000 km of rivers and canals.

The government aims to generate 20 percent of its electricity demand from renewable sources by 2030 and is promoting green industries and a national carbon market.
